content.text: {"answer":"For speeding up training with low-precision numbers, the supplied papers mainly cover distributed LLM training and on-device distributed learning, but not private federated training across user devices as a whole. On the low-precision side, FP4/NVFP4 training is presented as improving throughput, energy efficiency, speed, and memory, with mixed-precision recipes often needed to recover accuracy at scale [1, 2, 3]. Other work studies the tradeoff between FP and INT formats, finding FP often advantageous at 4-bit while fine-grained INT can be better in some 8-bit settings [5]. For distributed training, AGoQ uses near-4-bit activations plus 8-bit gradients and 8-bit All-Reduce to reduce memory and shorten communication time, improving LLM training speed while maintaining convergence [7].\n\nFor distributed private devices specifically, RockNet targets ultra-low-power devices and motivates on-device distributed learning partly by privacy concerns, reducing communication, memory, latency, and energy through specialized distributed training and wireless protocols [8]. A separate privacy-focused paper studies differentially private fine-tuning and shows that restoring low-rank gradient structure can speed DP optimization without weakening privacy guarantees, but it does not study low-precision arithmetic or distributed devices [6]. So the papers support a partial picture: low precision speeds large-scale distributed training [1, 2, 3, 7], and distributed on-device learning can help with privacy and efficiency [8], but none directly gives a comprehensive treatment of low-precision training across distributed private devices end to end [6, 8].","grounded":true}
